description: tonyd2wild's single-Spark vLLM TP1 profile for NVIDIA's own nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 checkpoint, used byte for byte (124 GB; 125B-A6B hybrid MoE, MTP head). The 47.7 GiB per-layer-embedding (n-gram) table stays on the NVMe and only the 16 rows each token needs are read on demand (disk-backed table patch, staged gather so decode runs as CUDA graphs), with a reduced-vocabulary MTP draft (65,536 ids), MTP 3, FP8 KV, memory utilization 0.80, 262,144 context, six sequences and 4,096-token prefill chunks (upstream defaults). The adapter bakes upstream's patch files and its vLLM overlays (PR #55375 fused PLE state-index fix, PR #54846 FP8/NVFP4 KV on the QSA path, and two ModelOpt MTP-loading fixes) into the image at upstream's exact vLLM commit 8a728663. Image note: upstream ran the vllm/vllm-openai nightly-8a728663 tag (CUDA 13.0.2), which is no longer on Docker Hub; the image installs the CUDA 13 wheel of the same vLLM commit (hash-locked) on NVIDIA's CUDA 13.0.2 base, so the SM12x kernels carry the family target GB10 loads, and a build-time scan fails the image if any does not. The disk-backed table needs the model files on a local NVMe (random reads over NFS crawl). Licences (information only): repository Apache-2.0; vLLM Apache-2.0; checkpoint under the NVIDIA Open Model License and the Qwen licence of the base model. Upstream figures (43.9 tok/s median single stream, 68.8 tok/s aggregate at six streams) are claims until measured here; alternatives from other creators: MiaAI-Lab's single-Spark vLLM and TensorFold kits. Vonk physical Spark acceptance is pending. GB10 memory correction: Per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus at least 8 GB for CUDA context/graphs, FlashInfer workspace, auxiliary heads and CPU/mmap buffers; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. This is a conservative budget, not a measured footprint.
title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 vLLM one Spark (tonyd2wild)
